question.name: CSEC Bio May 2022 Q5c — Sickle Cell Genetics: SS × SA Cross
question.text:
Sickle cell anaemia is a genetic disease. Use S to represent the sickle cell allele and A to represent the normal allele.

A person with sickle cell disease (SS) has a child with a person who has sickle cell trait (SA).

Draw a genetic diagram to show the possible genotypes and phenotypes of their offspring. (7 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Sickle cell genetics — SS × SA cross:

Alleles: S = sickle cell allele; A = normal allele

Genotypes and phenotypes:

  • SS = sickle cell disease (affected)
  • SA = sickle cell trait (carrier — usually healthy but can show mild symptoms under low oxygen conditions)
  • AA = normal (healthy)

Parents:

Sickle cell disease (SS) × Sickle cell trait (SA)

Gametes:

SS parent: S and S  |  SA parent: S and A

Punnett square:

S (from SS parent)S (from SS parent)
S (from SA parent)SSSS
A (from SA parent)SASA

Offspring genotypes: 50% SS : 50% SA (ratio 1:1)

Offspring phenotypes: 50% sickle cell disease : 50% sickle cell trait

Note: Every child has at least one S allele — none will be completely unaffected (AA).

steps.label:
Alleles: S = sickle cell allele | A = normal allele
SS = sickle cell disease | SA = sickle cell trait | AA = normal
Cross: SS parent × SA parent
Define alleles and state parent phenotypes. (2 marks)
State parent genotypes and gametes produced. (2 marks)
Complete Punnett square and state offspring genotypes and phenotypes. (3 marks)

fields.label: What does allele S represent? _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: S is the allele for the sickle cell form of haemoglobin.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: S represents the sickle cell allele (coding for abnormal haemoglobin HbS). A represents the normal allele (coding for normal haemoglobin HbA).

options.Sickle cell allele: Sickle cell allele (codes for abnormal HbS haemoglobin)
options.Normal allele: Normal allele (codes for normal HbA haemoglobin)

fields.label: Phenotype of the SS parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: A person with genotype SS has sickle cell disease (both alleles produce abnormal haemoglobin).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Genotype SS means both alleles are sickle cell alleles → the person has sickle cell disease (sickle cell anaemia). They produce only abnormal haemoglobin and suffer from the full disease.

fields.label: Phenotype of the SA parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: A person with genotype SA has sickle cell trait — they carry one sickle allele but are usually healthy (they produce both normal and abnormal haemoglobin).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Genotype SA means one sickle allele (S) and one normal allele (A). This gives sickle cell TRAIT — the person is a carrier. They are usually healthy under normal conditions.

fields.label: Gametes produced by the SS parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The SS parent can only produce gametes with the S allele (meiosis separates the two S alleles into separate gametes).

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The SS parent has two S alleles. During meiosis, alleles separate. So all gametes from the SS parent carry the S allele only.

options.A and A gametes: A and A gametes (only A gametes)

fields.label: Gametes produced by the SA parent = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: The SA parent produces two types of gametes: 50% with the S allele and 50% with the A allele.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The SA parent has one S allele and one A allele. During meiosis, these separate: 50% of gametes carry S and 50% carry A.

fields.label: Offspring genotypes from the Punnett square = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: From the Punnett square: SS parent gametes (S, S) × SA parent gametes (S, A) → SS, SS, SA, SA = 50% SS : 50% SA.

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Punnett square: (S and S) × (S and A) gives: S+S=SS, S+A=SA, S+S=SS, S+A=SA. Results: 2 SS and 2 SA → 50% SS : 50% SA.

fields.label: Offspring phenotypes and ratio = _____
fields.expected: 50% sickle cell disease : 50% sickle cell trait
fields.diagnostic_hint: All offspring have at least one S allele. 50% will have sickle cell disease (SS), 50% will have sickle cell trait (SA). No offspring will have the normal AA genotype.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: From the Punnett square: SS offspring → sickle cell disease; SA offspring → sickle cell trait. Ratio = 1 sickle cell disease : 1 sickle cell trait (50%:50%). No offspring will be completely normal (AA) because the SS parent can only pass on S alleles.

options.50% sickle cell disease : 50% sickle cel: 50% sickle cell disease : 50% sickle cell trait

fields.label: Describe how the Punnett square was set up (gametes on axes): _____
fields.expected: SS parent gametes (S,S) on one axis; SA parent gametes (S,A) on other axis
fields.diagnostic_hint: Set up the Punnett square with the SS parent gametes (S, S) on one axis and the SA parent gametes (S, A) on the other axis.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Label the Punnett square axes with parent gametes: SS parent contributes gametes S and S; SA parent contributes gametes S and A. Fill in the boxes by combining the alleles.

options.SS parent gametes (S,S) on one axis; SA: SS parent: S,S on one axis; SA parent: S,A on other axis
options.SS parent gametes (S,A) on one axis; SA: SS parent: S,A on one axis; SA parent: S,S on other axis
options.Both parents contribute only S gametes o: Both parents contribute only S gametes
